region: Northern Tanzania: Rift Valley, Ngorongoro and Serengeti
title: Tanzania — Calving Plains, Crater Rim and the Mountain of God
subtitle: Fourteen days of mobile camping from Tarangire to Ndutu and Lake Natron, timed for the wildebeest calving season
summary: A February camping safari through Tarangire, Ngorongoro, Ndutu, Seronera and the Rift Valley to Ol Doinyo Lengai. Outstanding wildlife and landscapes, but park fees and a private crew push the realistic total well above EUR 2,500 and post-election unrest keeps security conditional.
introduction: In February about half a million wildebeest calves are born on the short-grass plains around Ndutu, and the lions, cheetahs and hyenas that follow them make it one of the densest wildlife spectacles on the continent. The route begins in Tarangire among baobabs and elephants, climbs to the Ngorongoro rim at 2,300 m, and spends two nights in the southern Serengeti before the central Seronera valley and Olduvai Gorge. It then drops through Mto wa Mbu and Engaruka to the red soda shores of Lake Natron for a midnight climb of Ol Doinyo Lengai. Camp crews cook; local programmes host the Eyasi visits.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman was a self-drive desert and wadi journey with almost no wildlife. This is a vehicle-and-crew safari where the main event, the calving herds and their predators, is biological and time-limited, and where the group sleeps in unfenced public campsites with hyenas passing. Driving is by a hired driver-guide, not by the group.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: Package safaris sleep in lodges and move between pre-booked game-drive stops. Here the group camps in public campsites on the crater rim, Ndutu and the Seronera plain, walks a rim trail with a ranger, visits hunter-gatherers through a community programme and climbs an active volcano at night, with free days left for the herd's position.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: No other destination in the portfolio is built on a migratory wildlife event at ecosystem scale, and none combines calving-season savanna, a caldera, a World Heritage palaeoanthropology site and an active volcano in a single loop. It is also the most expensive Africa route in the portfolio.

duration.note: Day 1 outbound (arrive evening), day 13 evening departure, day 14 arrival in Paris.

recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: Mid-February sits in the peak calving window on the Ndutu plains (about 80% of births in 2-3 weeks), before the long rains that usually start in March. Natron and Engaruka tracks and Ndutu mud are least likely to be impassable then. Dates should be chosen after checking the herd's reported position and the rainfall pattern in January.

februarySuitability.summary: Peak calving and predator action on the southern plains, mostly dry between sporadic showers. Tarangire is in its quieter green season and Lengai ash is easier than in the wet.

marchSuitability.summary: Calving continues until about mid-March, but the long rains build with afternoon showers, grazing is depleted and the herds start moving north-west. Muddy tracks to Natron and Ndutu risk delays; low-season camp rates help only slightly.

climate.regionNote: Approximate climate normals across the route: Arusha (1,400 m), Ngorongoro rim (2,300 m), Serengeti/Ndutu (1,500 m) and Lake Natron (600 m). Not a 2027 forecast; figures are generic ranges from general climatology, not from a single retrieved station table.

february.rainfall: Typically a short drier spell between the short and long rains; sporadic showers, heavier in the afternoons on the highlands.
february.notes: Crater rim nights can be near 6 °C; Natron days exceed 34 °C.

march.rainfall: Long rains usually start mid- to late March; afternoon showers are building earlier, and tracks may become muddy.
march.notes: Mud on the Natron and Ndutu tracks is the main practical issue.

climate.snowAndMountainAccess: No snow on the route. Ngorongoro rim is cold and windy. Kilimanjaro climbs (not in the core route) are possible in January-early March.
climate.seaConditions: Not relevant: no coast on the core route.
climate.airQuality: Good in the parks; dust on dry tracks.
climate.wildlifeSeasonality: February is peak calving on the Ndutu plains with the herds concentrated in the south; Tarangire is in its green season with dispersed elephants; Lengai flamingo numbers at Natron vary with lake level and conditions.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Ramadan
holidaysAndFestivals.dates: about 8 February to 9 March 2027, moon-sighting dependent
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Affects Muslim-run businesses in Arusha and Zanzibar, not the parks, crater or Natron route.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Eid al-Fitr
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Public holiday; shops and buses limited around the day, outside the preferred window.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Easter weekend
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Outside the preferred window; long-rains start makes travel then less attractive.

climate.ramadan2027: Minor: not relevant to parks and crew. Some Arusha restaurants may close in daytime.
climate.tourismDemand: High season for calving: Ndutu and Serengeti campsites and operator vehicles book out months ahead. March is lower season.
climate.flightPriceSeasonality: Late January to March is generally lower demand for JRO than July-August; fares fluctuate with airline and connection city. Not verified for 2027.

geography.summary: The Gregory Rift Valley and its volcanic highlands, with savanna plains, soda lakes and an active volcano.
geography.distinctive: Ngorongoro is a 260 km2 caldera with a permanent wildlife population, Ndutu sits on the open plains where the herds calve, and Ol Doinyo Lengai is the only volcano in the world known to erupt natrocarbonatite lava.

landscapes.name: Ngorongoro Crater
landscapes.description: Collapsed volcano 600 m deep with a grassland, swamp and lake floor.

landscapes.name: Ndutu plains
landscapes.description: Short-grass plains where wildebeest and zebra calve in February.

landscapes.name: Lake Natron
landscapes.description: Alkaline soda lake under the Rift wall, red with microorganisms.

landscapes.name: Seronera valley
landscapes.description: Acacia and kopje country along the Seronera River.

culture.summary: Hadzabe, Datoga and Maasai communities, an early-human archaeological site and the market town of Mto wa Mbu; contact is through community programmes, not drive-by stops.

culturalHighlights.name: Olduvai Gorge
culturalHighlights.description: Where the Leakey team found early human fossils and tools; the museum explains the geology and discoveries.

culturalHighlights.name: Hadzabe visit at Lake Eyasi
culturalHighlights.description: A pre-dawn visit through the Lake Eyasi Cultural Tourism Programme. Photograph only with consent, bring no alcohol or tobacco, agree fees in advance and accept that the community's day sets the programme.

culturalHighlights.name: Datoga blacksmiths
culturalHighlights.description: A Datoga metalworking homestead near Mang'ola.

culturalHighlights.name: Mto wa Mbu market and farms
culturalHighlights.description: A town of more than 100 ethnic groups, with a produce market and irrigated farms.

culturalHighlights.name: Engaruka ruins
culturalHighlights.description: Stone-terraced irrigation fields of a pre-colonial farming settlement.

adventureHighlights.name: Ol Doinyo Lengai night climb
adventureHighlights.description: About 6-8 h round trip on steep loose ash, starting around midnight, with a local guide and a helmet.

adventureHighlights.name: Mobile camping in unfenced public campsites
adventureHighlights.description: Tents in Tarangire, Ngorongoro rim, Ndutu and Seronera; animals pass at night; food must be locked in the vehicle.

adventureHighlights.name: Ranger-led walk in the Ngorongoro highlands
adventureHighlights.description: A walk to Olmoti crater or on the rim with an armed ranger.

adventureHighlights.name: Optional: Kilimanjaro
adventureHighlights.description: Not part of the core route: a 6-7 day climb costs about USD 956 in park fees alone plus operator fees and does not fit with the safari in 14 days.

signatureExperiences.title: Calving season on the Ndutu plains
signatureExperiences.description: Two nights at Ndutu with full days among the wildebeest, zebras and gazelles with newborns, and the lions, cheetahs and hyenas that hunt them.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: The southern Serengeti is where the calving takes place; the timing, about 80% of births within 2-3 weeks in February, is rarely matched elsewhere.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Private camping safari with a driver-guide; book the Ndutu campsite and the crew months ahead; confirm the herd position with the operator the week before.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Entry for two NCA cycles plus campsite plus vehicle share, planning figure

signatureExperiences.title: Ngorongoro Crater at dawn after a night on the rim
signatureExperiences.description: Camp at 2,300 m, drop 600 m into the caldera at dawn and drive its grassland, forest and lake for six hours.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: One of the densest year-round concentrations of large mammals in Africa, including black rhinos, in a World Heritage setting.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: The crater service fee is per vehicle (USD 295, 6 hours maximum); the group shares it. Take an early slot to avoid the crowd.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Entry cycle plus crater fee share plus campsite

signatureExperiences.title: Ol Doinyo Lengai at night
signatureExperiences.description: Midnight start from the Natron side, summit at dawn over loose ash, with a view over Lake Natron.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: The only volcano known to erupt natrocarbonatite lava, with a steep climb that few safari itineraries include.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Local guide arranged through the Engare Sero community; helmets required; pre-arrange with the operator and check the volcano's activity.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Climb fee about USD 80-100 plus guide share

signatureExperiences.title: Lake Eyasi: hunter-gatherer and blacksmith visits
signatureExperiences.description: A pre-dawn visit with Hadzabe hunters and an afternoon with Datoga blacksmiths.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: One of the last hunter-gatherer groups in Africa; ethical practice (consent, no gifts, agreed fees) is part of the experience.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Via the registered Lake Eyasi Cultural Tourism Programme; agree fees in writing; decline staged performances.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Fees quoted USD 50-70 per person; sources conflict

travelStyle.summary: A private mobile-camping safari with a driver-guide and cook, local guides for walks and cultural visits, and unfenced campsites.

transport.summary: Everything is by 4x4 safari vehicle from Arusha; roads in the parks are dirt tracks. Domestic flights are not used.

modes.description: Pop-up-roof Land Cruiser for four with a driver-guide and a cook; standard for camping safaris.
Possible from Arusha rental firms (about USD 140-160/day); needs confidence on mud and tracks and local rules; not recommended for Ndutu in the wet.
In Mto wa Mbu and with rangers on the highlands.

transport.carRental: Self-drive 4x4 hire in Arusha runs USD 110-170 per day, rooftop-tent Land Cruisers USD 140-160; gear is extra and a few vehicle types are barred from Serengeti and Natron. Prices are from operator pages and should be confirmed in writing.

drivingRequirements.summary: Self-drive safari is possible but rare. Driving is on the left; roads outside towns are poor, and night driving is advised against by official sources.
drivingRequirements.internationalDrivingPermit: Rental firms generally ask for the national licence plus an international driving permit (1949 Geneva Convention); the exact Tanzanian legal requirement was not verified.
drivingRequirements.licenceNotes: Two of the four hold car licences and could share driving if the rental contract names additional drivers; the other two cannot drive.
drivingRequirements.motorcycleNotes: Nobody should ride a boda-boda or scooter without the correct licence; FCDO describes boda bodas and dala dalas as having poor safety records. Use the driver-guide vehicle, taxi or bicycle tours.
drivingRequirements.recommendedApproach: A hired driver-guide in a pop-up-roof 4x4 for the whole loop; self-drive is only the economical scenario.

accommodation.summary: Mostly campsites, with two Arusha nights/day rooms.

camping.summary: Eleven nights in tents with a cook. Public campsites are unfenced; animals pass at night. Crater-rim nights are cold.

physicalDifficulty.label: demanding
physicalDifficulty.summary: Long dusty days in the vehicle and cold, windy camps; the Lengai climb is a strenuous night ascent on ash. Altitude to 2,960 m.

itinerary.summary: Fourteen days: Tarangire, Mto wa Mbu, Lake Eyasi, Ngorongoro, Ndutu, Seronera, Olduvai, Engaruka and Lake Natron with a Lengai climb, ending in Arusha.

Visa and health-form checks at JRO
Transfer to the guesthouse

days.title: Markets, supplies and baobab country
activities: Morning at the Central Market: camp food and water
Meet crew, check vehicle, tents and kitchen kit
Drive to Tarangire; afternoon game drive
Night at the public campsite

days.title: Dawn drive and a market town
activities: Sunrise game drive inside Tarangire
Drive to Mto wa Mbu
Village walk or bicycle tour through banana farms and the market
Camp in the village

days.title: Into the hunter-gatherer basin
activities: Drive up through Karatu to Mang'ola
Visit Datoga blacksmiths and a homestead
Walk the lake shore at sunset
Camp near Mang'ola

activities: Pre-dawn visit with Hadzabe hunters (on their terms; no gifts of alcohol; ask before photographs)
Drive up to the Ngorongoro rim via Karatu
Afternoon walk and optional ranger-led Olmoti walk
Cold night at the rim campsite

Climb out and drive via Lemuta to Ndutu

Predators: lions, cheetahs, hyenas, jackals
Visit lakes Ndutu and Masek

Drive through kopjes to Seronera
Afternoon game drive
Camp at the public campsite

days.title: Leopards and the river
activities: Dawn and dusk drives along the Seronera River
Midday rest in camp
Optional hippo pool and kopjes visit
days.practical: Contingency day: if the herd or weather changes, the group can shift the plan.

days.title: Gorge of the first humans
activities: Leave at dawn via Naabi Hill gate
Olduvai Gorge museum and viewpoint
Drive up to Karatu

activities: Drive via Mto wa Mbu to Engaruka
Short walk through the Engaruka ruins
Continue to Lake Natron
Early night before the climb

activities: Start about 00:30 with a local guide; summit at dawn
Descent and rest
Afternoon walk in Engare Sero gorge and to the waterfall
Evening at the lake edge

Day room and shower, buy souvenirs
Transfer to JRO for the evening or night flight

days.title: Arrival in Paris
activities: Connect in Amsterdam (or other hub)
Arrive in Paris in the morning

stops.name: Kilimanjaro International Airport (JRO)
stops.description: Arrival and departure airport between Arusha and Moshi, with Kilimanjaro often visible from the apron on clear mornings.
activities: Visa check, health form, SIM card
Transfer to Arusha, about 1 h

stops.name: Arusha
stops.description: Safari gateway and base for supplies; Central Market, the Cultural Heritage Centre and the Maasai Market for food and camping provisions.
activities: Buy camp food and water at the Central Market and supermarkets
Briefing with the operator, vehicle and equipment check
Day room before the night flight
stops.culturalImportance: Regional trading town of the Meru and Maasai
stops.accommodation: Guesthouse, 2 twin rooms (night 1); day room on day 13
stops.costNote: Per person, guesthouse plus day room

stops.name: Tarangire National Park
stops.description: Baobab-studded park along the Tarangire River, known for large elephant herds. In February the park is in its green season, so game is more dispersed than in the dry months.
activities: Full-day game drive from the river outward
Night at the public campsite with elephants and hyenas passing at night
Bird-watching in the green season

stops.name: Mto wa Mbu
stops.description: Farming town at the foot of the Rift Valley escarpment, home to people from more than 100 ethnic groups, with a produce market and banana-and-rice farms below Lake Manyara.
activities: Village walk or bicycle tour through the banana plantations and market
Watch the escarpment from a rooftop
Camp in the village

stops.name: Lake Eyasi (Mang'ola)
stops.description: Alkaline lake in the Rift Valley bordered by Hadzabe and Datoga communities; the group visits through the registered Lake Eyasi Cultural Tourism Programme.
activities: Datoga blacksmiths and homestead visit
Pre-dawn visit with Hadzabe hunters, on their schedule, with consent-based photography
Sunset by the lake
stops.geography: Shallow salt lake, hot and dry basin
stops.costNote: Cultural programme and local guide fees

stops.name: Ngorongoro Crater rim and highlands
stops.description: Camp on the crater rim at about 2,300 m, then a descent into the caldera for a 6-hour game drive. A ranger-led walk in the Olmoti highlands is the optional walking day.
activities: Afternoon rim walk and sunset
Early descent: rhinos, lions, hippos, flamingo flocks on Lake Magadi
Optional ranger-led walk to Olmoti crater (armed ranger required)
stops.culturalImportance: UNESCO World Heritage mixed site; Maasai pastoralists share the conservation area
stops.accommodation: NCAA campsite on the rim, cold nights
stops.costNote: Entry USD 70.80 + campsite USD 59 + crater fee share

stops.name: Ndutu (Lake Ndutu and Ndutu plains)
stops.description: Short-grass plains on the southern edge of the Serengeti ecosystem, inside the Ngorongoro Conservation Area, where wildebeest give birth in the first months of the year.
activities: Full day with the calving herds and the predators that follow them
Visit Lake Masek and Lake Ndutu woodlands
Camp in the Ndutu woods, with hyena and genet visits
stops.geography: Short-grass plains and acacia woodland, about 1,500 m
stops.transport: Safari vehicle on tracks that turn to mud in rain

stops.name: Seronera, central Serengeti
stops.description: Seronera valley has the highest density of leopards and lions in the park, with kopjes and river woodland. The public campsite sits in the middle of the wildlife corridor.
activities: Dawn and dusk drives along the Seronera River
Search for leopards in sausage trees
Hippo pool and kopje walk viewpoints
stops.geography: Acacia savanna and granite kopjes, 1,500 m

stops.name: Olduvai Gorge
stops.description: Gorge where Louis and Mary Leakey found early human fossils and stone tools; a small museum explains the strata.
activities: Museum and guided walk to the viewing platform
Gorge overlook

stops.name: Karatu
stops.description: Farming town on the Ngorongoro highlands road, with campsites and coffee farms.
activities: Restock at the market
Rest night after the Serengeti drive

stops.name: Engaruka ruins
stops.description: Ruins of an irrigated agricultural settlement with stone-walled terraces, occupied from the 15th to the 18th century; little visited.
activities: Short guided walk through the terraces and canals
stops.geography: Rift escarpment foot with a view of Lengai

stops.name: Lake Natron (Engare Sero)
stops.description: Alkaline soda lake under the Rift wall, red with cyanobacteria; shore camp near the Engare Sero stream and gorge.
activities: Walk in Engare Sero gorge and to the waterfall
Flamingo and bird viewing on the lake edge
Camp on the shore

assumptions: USD fees converted at about EUR 0.86 per USD (planning assumption, not a quote); 18% VAT is included in park fees.
Realistic = private guided camping safari with driver-guide and cook; economical = self-drive 4x4 with rooftop tents; comfortable = guided with lodge or tented-camp nights.
Park and conservation fees are 2026 tariffs; 2027 values are not published and may change in July 2026-2027 reviews.
Vehicle-entry fees, mandatory inbound insurance premium and crew rates are estimates.
budget.exceptionalJustification: The realistic total is far above the EUR 2,500 ceiling because park and conservation fees alone are about EUR 700 per person for 7 park-days plus a private vehicle, cook and camping crew; no credible cheaper private variant exists for the calving-season Serengeti loop. Shared (group-joining) camping safaris may be cheaper but remove independence.

scenarioNotes.economical: Self-drive 4x4 with rooftop tents, no cook or tips; still above EUR 2,500 once fees and flights are included.
scenarioNotes.realistic: Private guided camping safari: driver-guide vehicle, cook and crew, public campsites, community-programme visits and Lengai guide.
scenarioNotes.comfortable: Guided safari with six nights in lodges or tented camps, higher-end flights and crew tips.

security.summary: Official advice conflicts in tone: France, UK, Netherlands and Australia do not advise against the northern safari route (only the Mozambique border area is warned against), but the US reportedly rates Tanzania Level 3 Reconsider travel after the unrest around the 29 October 2025 election, and France warns of hard-to-predict demonstrations, possible curfews and internet cuts. The route avoids the red/orange zones.
security.assessedRoute: Arusha, Tarangire, Mto wa Mbu, Lake Eyasi, Ngorongoro, Ndutu, Serengeti (Seronera), Olduvai, Engaruka and Lake Natron. Not assessed: Dar es Salaam, Zanzibar, Mtwara, Lindi, Ruvuma, Kagera and Kigoma.

advisories.level: Yellow (vigilance renforcée) for the north (Arusha, Kilimanjaro); red for Mtwara and the Mozambique border; orange for Kagera, Kigoma, Lindi and Ruvuma

advisories.routeImpact: None of the route regions are orange or red

advisories.level: Yellow for the country; orange only for Mtwara region (page updated 27 November 2026)

conflictRisk.note: Post-election demonstrations in October-November 2025 turned violent; further unrest is possible. The northern safari circuit is far from the Cabo Delgado insurgency.

terrorismRisk.note: FCDO: attacks cannot be ruled out; Al-Shabaab-linked extremists thought active; IS-Mozambique risk near Cabo Delgado only.

kidnappingRisk.note: Express kidnapping reported in Dar es Salaam, not on the route; kidnapping risk in the Mozambique border region is outside the route.

regionalRestrictions: Do not enter the Mtwara, Lindi, Ruvuma, Kagera or Kigoma areas.
Avoid demonstrations; filming or posting protests can be illegal.
Check the Ebola situation in the DRC; online health declaration and entry checks apply.
ordinaryRisks: Bag snatching and robbery in cities; hotel burglary
Wildfires, flooding and impassable tracks in rain
Hippos, buffaloes and hyenas at camp
security.medicalAccess: Limited outside Dar es Salaam; Arusha has private hospitals; evacuation insurance is necessary for remote camps and Lengai. Emergency number 112.
security.insuranceConsiderations: France Diplomatie reports mandatory Tanzanian inbound insurance since 1 October 2026. FCDO notes that insurance may be invalidated if travelling against FCDO advice; the US Level 3 may affect some policies. Confirm unrest exclusions and evacuation cover.
security.reassessmentRequired: Re-check all advisories before booking and two weeks before departure. Triggers: new curfews or internet shutdowns, US or French upgrades above current levels, violence near Arusha, fuel shortages, Ebola in Tanzania, flooding from El Niño.

practicalRequirements.visa: Tourist visa required for most nationalities; e-visa before travel at about USD 50 single entry (USD 100 multiple); confirm for each passport.
practicalRequirements.entry: Return or onward ticket, Travellers Health Surveillance Form, mandatory inbound insurance, health checks (mpox/Ebola screening).
practicalRequirements.passportValidity: At least 6 months after arrival and one blank page.
permits: Lengai climbing permit through the Engare Sero community
Park entry via operator or TanapaGo
practicalRequirements.insurance: Travel insurance with medical evacuation, trekking and safari cover, plus the mandatory local policy.
practicalRequirements.connectivity: SIM cards in Arusha; coverage is patchy in the parks and none at Natron or Ndutu in places; internet cuts are possible during unrest.
practicalRequirements.payments: Mostly cash (USD notes printed 2013 or later and Tanzanian shillings) in villages; cards in Arusha; park fees are prepaid via the operator.
practicalRequirements.medical: Malaria prophylaxis recommended; yellow fever certificate required only if arriving from a risk country (transit through Nairobi or Addis should be checked); routine vaccinations; altitude awareness at the rim and Lengai.
practicalRequirements.fuel: Diesel is available in Arusha, Karatu and Mto wa Mbu; FCDO notes shortages after the election.
equipment: Warm layers for the crater rim (6 °C)

advantages: Calving season concentrates huge wildlife and predator action in one place.
Camping gives access to dawn and dusk light and quiet nights inside parks.
Cultural contact through registered community programmes and Olduvai gives depth beyond wildlife.
Ol Doinyo Lengai and the crater rim add real adventure.
Official advice covers only the Mozambique border area with a warning for specific regions.
disadvantages: Realistic total is far above EUR 2,500; flights, park fees and a private crew drive it.
Post-election unrest and the US Level 3 keep security conditional.
Very long days on dusty roads, much of the trip in a vehicle.
Wildlife viewing is mostly from vehicles; walking is rare.
Hadzabe visits carry real ethical risk of staged, paid performances.
uncertainties: 2027 park fees and vehicle fees are unpublished; 2026 operator-quoted tariffs are used.
Current US advisory level and whether further unrest follows the post-election period.
El Niño flooding and landslides (France alert 2 Nov 2026) could disrupt Ndutu, Natron and Engaruka tracks.
Exact flight prices for February 2027 and 2027 operator quotations.

claims: Situation sécuritaire since the October 2025 elections: violent protests in Oct–Nov 2025; risk of hard-to-predict demonstrations in major cities, partial or total internet cuts, shortages of fuel/food/water lasting several days, possible curfews; no curfew currently reported
Mandatory local travel insurance for foreign visitors since 1 October 2026 (page updated 12 November 2026)
Ebola outbreak in DRC: no case declared in Tanzania, stricter entry health checks; El Niño alert of 2 November 2026 (floods, landslides)

sources.title: Tanzanie – Conseils aux voyageurs – Sécurité
claims: Red (formellement déconseillé): Mozambique border and Mtwara region; orange (déconseillé sauf raison impérative): Kagera, Kigoma, Lindi, Ruvuma; yellow (vigilance renforcée) for the rest of the country including Arusha and Kilimanjaro
Avoid night driving outside towns; high road accident rates; do not leave the vehicle in wildlife parks; Kilimanjaro and Meru climbs require reputable guides and rescue insurance
Crime rising in tourist areas; EU ban on Tanzanian airlines noted

sources.title: Foreign travel advice Tanzania
claims: FCDO advises against all but essential travel only to parts of Tanzania: any area within 20 km of the Cabo Delgado (Mozambique) border; the rest of the country has no such warning

sources.title: Tanzania – Safety and security
